entry.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; alternatives from JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 recorded in commentary
entry.wohChoice: 22:1, 5 gêʾ ḥizzāyôn 'the valley of vision', lower case (ASV; wave ruling 7). 22:3 miqqešeṯ ʾussārû 'they were bound by the archers' (ASV; the privative 'without the bow' of JPS 1917 / NJPS in commentary). 22:4 baṯ-ʿammî 'the daughter of my people' (ASV, JPS 1917; the appositional sense in commentary); ʾāmartî past, 'Therefore I said'. 22:5 possessive lᵉ: 'For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of tumult …', concordant with 2:12 (NJPS; changed from the draft's ASV 'from the Lord'); mᵉqarqar qir wᵉšôaʿ ʾel-hāhār 'a breaking down of the wall, and a crying to the mountain', common nouns in MT's singular (Kir / Shoa as peoples, JPS 1917 / NJPS, in commentary). 22:6 'with chariots of men and horsemen' ('and' supplied, as ASV; ʾāḏām = 'men' for a body of fighting men under wave ruling 13). 22:8 'he took away the covering of Judah' (ASV; subject unexpressed); bêṯ hayyaʿar 'the house of the forest', lower case (ASV). 22:13 'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die' (ASV, JPS 1917). 22:14 'YHWH of hosts revealed himself in my ears' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS). 22:15 hassōḵēn 'this treasurer' (ASV; 'steward' recorded as the closer gloss). PENDING FOUNDER RULING: staged alternative line 'Go, get you to this steward, to Shebna, who is over the house:' (JPS 1917, NJPS 'steward'; Reviewer recommends 'steward', Editor recommended keeping 'treasurer'); if adopted, this clause becomes hassōḵēn 'this steward' and the line changes with it; ʾăšer ʿal-habbāyiṯ 'who is over the house'; ASV's supplied '[and say]' not added. 22:16 third-person suffixes kept with ASV alone, 'hewing out his tomb on high … for himself' (JPS 1917 and NJPS both convert to the second person); qeḇer 'tomb'. 22:17 'hurl you away violently, like a strong man; and he will wrap you up closely' (ASV, brackets dropped). 22:18 'He will surely wind you round and round, like a ball' (ASV without its supplied verb); markᵉḇôṯ kᵉḇôḏeḵā 'the chariots of your glory'; ʾăḏōneyḵā 'your lord', lower case. 22:19 yehersᵉḵā rendered as a passive, 'you shall be pulled down' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS; MT third person in commentary). 22:21 kuttōneṯ 'robe', ʾaḇnēṭ 'girdle', memšālāh 'government' (ASV; NJPS 'tunic', 'sash', 'authority' in commentary). 22:22 'the key of the house of David', singular. 22:18, 23, 24 kāḇôḏ in non-divine constructs = 'glory' (wave ruling 2, strict): 'the chariots of your glory', 'a throne of glory', 'all the glory of his father's house'. 22:24 'the offspring and the issue'; ʾaggānôṯ 'cups', nᵉḇālîm 'flagons' (nēḇel II, distinct from nēḇel I 'harp' at 5:12; 14:11); the repeated kᵉlê kept with JPS 1917. 22:25 hammaśśāʾ (maśśāʾ I 'load') 'the burden' (ASV, JPS 1917), not governed by massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah.
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Hebrew is rare, elliptical or ambiguous. The line keeps a standard public-domain rendering, usually ASV and often shared by JPS 1917, and the commentary reports the alternatives; one item departs from ASV. (a) 22:5: after yôm, the preposition lᵉ with the divine name is the possessive construction of 2:12 (kî yôm laYHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ), which the stable chapter prints as 'there is a day of YHWH of hosts'. ASV and JPS 1917 render lᵉ as 'from', a sense the preposition rarely has. NJPS reads possession ('my Lord GOD of Hosts had a day'), and NRSV is recalled as doing the same, not verified. The line therefore reads 'For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of …', which keeps the two verses concordant and adds nothing to the Hebrew. (b) kāḇôḏ at 22:18, 23, 24 refers to human status and possessions. Wave ruling 2 makes 'glory' strict for kāḇôḏ in every use, as the stable 10:3, 10:18 and 11:10 already show. ASV and JPS 1917 print 'glory' at 22:18 and 22:24 and ASV at 22:23, so the rule costs nothing against the baseline. The departures of JPS 1917 ('throne of honour') and NJPS ('seat of honor', 'substance', 'chariots bearing your body') are reported. 1 Sam 2:8 has the same kissēʾ kāḇôḏ, rendered 'the throne of glory' by ASV. (c) 22:6: ʾāḏām qualifies chariotry and refers to the crews of an army. Wave ruling 13 limits the gender-neutral rule of adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah to generic human nouns, so 'men' is kept. The remaining items follow ASV where the Hebrew admits it. At 22:3 both the agentive and the privative min are attested, and NJPS marks the line as uncertain. At 22:4 baṯ-ʿammî is the appositional genitive of baṯ-ṣiyyôn (1:8); the literal form keeps the personification, and NJPS gives the same sense in its note ('the young woman, my people'). The phrase is frequent in Jeremiah and Lamentations, and promotion to the central glossary is recommended when those books are drafted. At 22:5 the Kir / Shoa reading of JPS 1917 and NJPS is a recognised alternative (NJPS: 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'); MT's singular nouns are kept against ASV's plurals. At 22:15 sōḵēn occurs only here as an office title. Its Ugaritic and Phoenician cognates (skn, 'prefect') favour JPS 1917 / NJPS 'steward' (HALOT; recalled, not verified), but ASV 'treasurer' is a standard rendering and is kept as the baseline pending the founder's ruling (PENDING FOUNDER RULING; the staged alternative line is given in wohChoice). The Reviewer recommends 'steward', noting that 'treasurer' probably descends from the LXX ταμίας (recalled, not verified). At 22:16, 19 the changes of person are MT's. The line keeps the third person at 22:16 with ASV alone (JPS 1917 'Thou that hewest thee out a sepulchre on high' and NJPS 'O you who have hewn your tomb on high' both convert to the second person) and follows all three references in rendering the indefinite third person of 22:19 as a passive, an ordinary English rendering of an impersonal subject. At 22:17-18 ASV's bracketed supplements ('[strong]', '[and toss thee]') are dropped or absorbed. The words are rare (ṭalṭēlāh; ṣᵉnēp̄āh; ʿṭh, possibly ʿṭh II 'grasp'), and the alternatives are reported. At 22:21 'girdle' and 'government' are kept with ASV, although the stable chapters use 'girdle' for ʾēzôr (11:5) and ḥăḡôrāh (3:24) and 'government' for miśrāh (9:5). The collisions are stated in commentary instead of being removed by a new gloss. At 22:24 ṣᵉp̄iʿôṯ occurs only here, and ASV's 'issue' is kept. At 22:25 the noun is maśśāʾ I 'load', not the heading noun maśśāʾ II of 22:1, and 'burden' is the ordinary English. The entry is direct, because every rendering is attested in ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS and no reading is added.

entry.strongs: H3489 (yāṯēḏ); with H8628 (tāqaʿ 'drive in, fasten'). Numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: yāṯēḏ 'peg, pin, stake' (tent peg; wall peg; digging tool, Deut 23:14)
entry.standardEnglish: ASV 'nail' (Isa 22:23, 25; Ezra 9:8), 'stakes' (Isa 54:2), 'pin' (Judg 4:21; Ezek 15:3); JPS 1917 and NJPS 'peg' (Isa 22:23, 25)
entry.wohChoice: 'peg' where the yāṯēḏ is driven in to hold or carry a weight (22:23, 25: 'I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place'; 'the peg that was fastened in a sure place'). Context clause: 'stake(s)' for the pegs of a tent (54:2 'strengthen your stakes', stable, already so printed; 33:20 when drafted). Never 'nail', which in modern English denotes a metal fastener.
entry.rationale: A yāṯēḏ is a pointed wooden or metal peg. It is driven into the ground to hold a tent (Judg 4:21; Exod 27:19), into a wall to hang things on (Ezek 15:3, 'a pin to hang any vessel thereon', ASV), or carried as a digging tool (Deut 23:14) (BDB; HALOT). In Isa 22:23-25 the image is a peg driven (tqʿ) into a firm place, on which the household's vessels are hung (22:24). JPS 1917 and NJPS render it 'peg', and so does this entry. ASV's 'nail' reflects older English usage, but a modern reader takes it for a metal nail hammered flat. The stable 54:2 prints the tent sense as 'stakes', the normal English for tent pegs, and the entry keeps that wording as a context clause instead of changing a stable line. One Hebrew word therefore has two English renderings divided by context, and both are standard glosses. The entry is direct because both renderings are the ordinary lexical senses attested in the public-domain versions. Orchestrator: ISA-54:2 is in a stable chapter, so its glossaryRefs need the new id when the diff is merged; its English line is unchanged.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-4 (Isa 22): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 22 — The oracle concerning the valley of vision, and the key of the house of David given from Shebna to Eliakim' is kept. Quotation marks enclose the prophet's words at 22:4 and the revelers' words at 22:13, the same extents as JPS 1917 (checked on Sefaria). Divine speech after 'revealed himself in my ears' (22:14) and after the messenger formula (22:15-25) is not in quotation marks; ASV's supplied '[and say]' at 22:15 is not added. 'YHWH' house style at 22:17, 25.

Wave I-4 (Isa 22): 22:1 maśśāʾ gêʾ ḥizzāyôn 'The oracle concerning the valley of vision' (ASV 'The burden of', JPS 1917 'The burden concerning', NJPS 'Pronouncement'). Scope note: the entry governs maśśāʾ II in headings only. At 22:25 hammaśśāʾ ʾăšer-ʿālehā is maśśāʾ I, a 'load', and the line has 'the burden' (ASV, JPS 1917) under lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22. The 'burden in commentary only' clause does not reach maśśāʾ I. The chapter's play between its heading and its last noun is described in the 22:25 commentary.

Wave I-4 (Isa 22): laʾḏōnāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ (22:5), ʾăḏōnāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ (22:12, 14, 15) 'the Lord YHWH of hosts'. At 22:5 the lᵉ is possessive ('the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day'), under lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22.

Wave I-4 (Isa 22): 22:14 ʾim-yᵉḵuppar heʿāwōn hazzeh lāḵem, a Pual imperfect in an oath formula, 'Surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die'. ASV and NJPS have 'forgiven' and JPS 1917 'expiated'. 'Atoned for' keeps the kpr verb concordant with 6:7 and 27:9.

Wave I-4 (Isa 22): 22:11 yōṣᵉrāh mērāḥôq 'the one who formed it long ago'. This is the suffixed participle with God as subject, so its verbal force is kept, and the parallel ʿōśêhā is matched as 'the one who made it'. The feminine suffix has no stated antecedent (the city, the reservoir, or the event). ASV 'him that purposed it' and NJPS 'Him who designed it' read the planning sense of yṣr, as at 37:26, and are reported in commentary.

Wave I-4 ruling 13 (scope): the gender-neutral rule governs generic human nouns only. Nouns for a specific body of male fighters keep 'men'. At 22:6 bᵉreḵeḇ ʾāḏām pārāšîm 'with chariots of men and horsemen', ʾāḏām names the crews or troops of the Elamite force, and the verse is not governed by this entry (recorded in lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22).
